issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking a declaration of ownership is not maintainable when the defendant possesses part of the disputed property and the plaintiff omits to seek possession of it.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought a declaration of ownership but did not seek possession of any part of the property.
The defendant was found to possess property that had been in the possession of the deceased co-owner.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not maintainable because the plaintiffs sought only a declaration and omitted the consequential relief of possession.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, a declaratory suit is not maintainable when the plaintiff is able to seek further relief but omits to do so. The Court relied on no earlier cases in deciding this issue.

predicates.declaratory_ownership_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking a declaration of ownership of disputed property.
predicates.defendant_possesses_disputed_property: The defendant possesses at least part of the disputed property.
predicates.plaintiff_omitted_possession_relief: The plaintiff did not seek possession of the part of the disputed property possessed by the defendant.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff seeks a declaration of ownership, the defendant possesses disputed property, and the plaintiff omits to seek possession, the declaratory suit is not maintainable.
